Medcity|Aster Pharmacy|Aster Labs|Dr. Moopen's Medical College}} | website = {{URL|asterdmhealthcare.in}} }} '''Aster DM Healthcare Limited''' is an Indian healthcare company founded by [[Azad Moopen]] in 1987. The company is registered in [[Bengaluru]], which became the headquarters for its India operations following the separation of its [[Gulf Cooperation Council]] (GCC) business in 2024. Aster operates a network of hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and diagnostic centres across several Indian states.{{Cite web |title=India's Strategic Expansion and Merge Fuels Growth |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.docs//Aster%20DM%20-%20IC%20-%20HSIE-202506201055355322533.pdf?t=21062025120057057 |website=HDFC Sec}} == History == Aster DM Healthcare was established by [[Azad Moopen]] in 1987 as a single-doctor clinic.{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Lalatendu |date=2019-12-21 |title='We're adding one hospital in India every year' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/were-adding-one-hospital-in-india-every-year/article30368808.ece |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} The organisation gradually expanded through hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, diagnostics, and training institutions.{{cite web |date=12 December 2013 |title=Aster Launches Access Clinic in Jafza |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-352688245.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115054523/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-352688245.html |archive-date=15 November 2018 |accessdate=19 June 2014 |newspaper=[[Khaleej Times]]}} Its formal presence in India began in 2001 with the [[Aster MIMS|Malabar Institute of Medical Sciences]] (MIMS) in [[Kozhikode|Kozhikode, Kerala]], which was later integrated into the Aster network.{{Cite web |date=2011-03-24 |title=Dr Azad Moopen to be presented Padma Shri |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/dr-azad-moopen-to-be-presented-padma-shri/ |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Aster DM Healthcare Ltd. |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/HSL_Pick%20of%20the%20week%20-%20Aster%20DM%20Healthcare%20281024%20Final%20Signed.pdf |website=HDFC Securities (research report)}}{{cite web |date=24 April 2014 |title=Aster DM Healthcare to Start Helpdesks in Oman |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-367098294.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924154826/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-367098294.html |archive-date=24 September 2015 |accessdate=19 June 2014 |magazine=[[The Week (Indian magazine)|The Week]]}} In 2014, the company opened Aster Medcity in [[Kochi]].{{Cite news |date=2023-11-28 |title=Aster DM sells stake in its Gulf business for $1.01 billion |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/aster-dm-sells-stake-in-its-gulf-business-for-1-01-billion/articleshow/105568929.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} In 2016, it acquired Kavery Medical Institute in Bengaluru, redeveloping it as Aster CMI Hospital.{{Cite news |date=2014-09-12 |title=IPO-bound Aster strikes deals for B'lore, Hyderabad foray |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/ipo-bound-aster-strikes-deals-for-blore-hyderabad-foray/articleshow/42296911.cms |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} The same year, it took over the DM Wayanad Institute of Medical Sciences{{Cite web |date=2019-04-06 |title=First batch of doctors graduates from Wayanad Medical College |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/kochi/2019/Apr/05/first-batch-of-doctors-graduates-from-wayanad-medical-college-1960797.html |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} and acquired a majority stake in Dr. Ramesh Hospitals in Andhra Pradesh.{{Cite web |title=Aster DM Healthcare picking majority stake in PE-backed Ramesh Hospitals |url=https://www.vccircle.com/exclusive-aster-dm-healthcare-picking-majority-stake-pe-backed |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=VCCircle |language=en-US}} In 2018, Aster added Sangamitra Hospitals to its network{{Cite web |date=2018-04-01 |title=Ramesh Hospitals acquires Ongole's Sanghamitra Hospital |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/andhra-pradesh/2018/Apr/01/ramesh-hospitals-acquires-ongoles-sanghamitra-hospital-1795432.html |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} and launched an [[initial public offering]], with shares subsequently listed on Indian stock exchanges. New facilities established in the following years included Aster MIMS Kannur and Aster RV Hospital in Bengaluru in 2019.{{Cite web |last=Varghese |first=Joseph |date=2019-12-25 |title=Aster India offers quality medical tourism for Qataris, residents |url=https://www.gulf-times.com/story/651637/aster-india-offers-quality-medical-tourism-for-qataris-residents |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=Gulf Times |language=en}} In 2021, the company opened a hospital in Kottakkal focused on women and children, followed by Aster Whitefield in Bengaluru in 2023.{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Neetu Chandra |date=2021-11-25 |title='Our India strategy involves focused clusters and new revenue streams' {{!}} Today News |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/our-india-strategy-involves-focused-clusters-and-new-revenue-streams-11637782106976.html |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=mint |language=en}} In November 2023, Aster DM Healthcare announced a plan to separate its GCC and India businesses, approved by shareholders in January 2024 and completed in April 2024, when a consortium led by [[Fajr Capital]] acquired a 65% stake in the GCC business — now operating independently as [[Aster DM Healthcare FZC]] (trading as Aster Hospitals & Clinics, whose hospital operations across the UAE, Oman and Bahrain are led by [[Sherbaz Bichu|Dr. Sherbaz Bichu]] as Chief Executive Officer).{{cite news |title=Aster DM sells stake in its Gulf business for $1.01 billion |work=The Economic Times |date=28 November 2023 |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/aster-dm-sells-stake-in-its-gulf-business-for-1-01-billion/articleshow/105568929.cms}}{{cite news |title=Aster DM healthcare separates its GCC and India operations |work=The Times of India |date=4 April 2024 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/aster-dm-healthcare-separates-its-gcc-and-india-operations/articleshow/109043777.cms |issn=0971-8257}}{{cite news |title=Aster Royal Al Raffah opens cancer centre |work=Oman Observer |date=6 March 2025 |url=https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1167299/oman/aster-royal-al-raffah-opens-cancer-centre}} The Moopen family retained a 35% stake in the GCC business and operational control, while continuing to hold a 41.88% stake in Aster DM Healthcare in India; the company's subsidiary, Affinity Holdings, received US$907.6 million from the transaction.{{cite news |title=Aster DM Healthcare shares fall 7% amid block deal |work=Fortune India |date=27 March 2024 |first=Chitranjan |last=Kumar |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/investing/aster-dm-healthcare-shares-fall-7-amid-block-deal/116257}} [[Alisha Moopen]], daughter of founder [[Azad Moopen]], serves as Managing Director and Group CEO of the separated GCC business, Aster DM Healthcare FZC.{{cite web |title=Ms. Alisha Moopen {{!}} Managing Director & Group CEO |url=https://www.astermedicalimaging.com/our-leaders/alisha-moopen/ |publisher=Aster Medical Imaging |access-date=2026-07-18}} {{Main|Aster DM Healthcare FZC}} In November 2024, Aster announced a merger with Quality Care India Ltd. (QCIL),{{Cite news |date=2024-11-30 |title=Aster DM Healthcare, Quality Care India ink merger deal |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/aster-dm-healthcare-quality-care-india-ink-merger-deal/articleshow/115826289.cms |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}{{Cite web |date=2024-11-30 |title=With 14,000 beds, we will become one of the largest healthcare providers in India, says Alish Moopen - BusinessToday |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/with-14000-beds-we-will-become-one-of-the-largest-healthcare-providers-in-india-says-alish-moopen-455745-2024-11-30 |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=Business Today |language=en}} to form Aster DM Quality Care Ltd.{{Cite news |date=2024-11-29 |title=Aster and quality care merge to create one of the top 3 hospital chains in India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/aster-and-quality-care-merge-to-create-one-of-the-top-3-hospital-chains-in-india/articleshow/115816115.cms |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}{{Cite news |last=Mishra |first=Lalatendu |date=2024-11-30 |title='Our goal is to become the finest healthcare institution in India' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/our-goal-is-to-become-the-finest-healthcare-institution-in-india/article68931383.ece |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} In 2025, the company opened a 100-bed hospital in [[Sharjah]]{{Cite web |title=Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi inaugurates Aster Hospital Sharjah |url=https://www.wam.ae/en/article/hszrfp0u-sultan-bin-ahmed-qasimi-inaugurates-aster-hospital |website=Emirates News Agency}} and a 264-bed Aster MIMS hospital in [[Kasaragod]], [[Kerala]].{{Cite news |date=2025-10-02 |title=Aster DM Healthcare launches ₹190-crore multispecialty hospital in Kasaragod |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/aster-dm-healthcare-launches-195-crore-multispecialty-hospital-in-kasaragod/article70117772.ece |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} It increased its stake in Dr. Ramesh Cardiac and Multispecialty Hospital Private Limited to 70.49%.{{Cite web |date=2025-09-03 |title=Aster DM Healthcare acquires additional 13% stake in Aster Ramesh Hospitals |url=https://www.expresshealthcare.in/news/aster-dm-healthcare-acquires-additional-13-stake-in-aster-ramesh-hospitals/450496/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |website=Express Healthcare |language=en-US}} == Investors == In 2012, Olympus Capital Holdings Asia acquired a minority stake in Aster DM Healthcare for about {{USD}}100 million, becoming the company’s largest external investor.{{cite web |author=Joshi, Ashutosh |date=18 January 2012 |title=Olympus Capital Buys DM Healthcare Stake for $100 Million |url=https://blogs.wsj.com/dealjournalindia/2012/01/18/olympus-capital-buys-dm-healthcare-stake-for-100-million/ |accessdate=19 June 2014 |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]]}} In May 2014, Olympus invested an additional {{USD}}60 million.{{cite web |author=Cheung, Sonja |date=14 May 2014 |title=Asian Private Equity Fund Face Pressure to Invest Capital Hoard |url=https://blogs.wsj.com/privateequity/2014/05/14/asian-private-equity-fund-face-pressure-to-invest-capital-hoard/ |accessdate=19 June 2014 |newspaper=The Wall Street Journal}} Olympus exited its investment in June 2024. Following the GCC–India separation, the Moopen family continues to hold 41.88% of the Indian business.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=3 April 2024 |title=Aster DM Healthcare concludes separation of India and GCC businesses |url=https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/aster-dm-healthcare-concludes-separation-of-india-and-gcc-businesses-124040300562_1.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524102202/https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/aster-dm-healthcare-concludes-separation-of-india-and-gcc-businesses-124040300562_1.html |archive-date=2024-05-24 |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Business Standard |language=en-US}}{{Cite news |last=Pilla |first=Viswanath |date=2024-04-03 |title=Aster DM completes separation of Gulf business, plans to add 1,700 beds in India in next 3 years |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/healthcare/aster-dm-completes-separation-of-gulf-business-plans-to-add-1700-beds-in-india-in-next-3-years/articleshow/109003741.cms |access-date=2024-12-27 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} == Subsidiaries == [[File:Aster_MIMS_Kannur.jpg|thumb|[[Aster MIMS]] in [[Kannur]]]] [[File:Aster_Medcity_Hospital_Entrance.jpg|thumb|[[Aster Medcity]] in [[Kochi]]]] Aster DM Healthcare operates through multiple subsidiaries and affiliates, including 9 subsidiaries, 67 step-down subsidiaries, and 4 associate companies. Notable operations include: *'''Aster Capital, Trivandrum''' is an upcoming multi-specialty hospital project in the capital city [[Trivandrum]] developed as part of the Aster healthcare network. The hospital is planned as a large super-specialty facility with advanced medical infrastructure and a wide range of clinical specialties including cardiology, oncology, neurology, orthopedics, and transplant services. Once operational, it is expected to significantly strengthen the private healthcare ecosystem in the capital region by improving access to high-quality tertiary care and modern medical technologyhttps://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/aster-dm-to-launch-healthcare-facility-in-trivandrum/92293377 * '''Aster Medcity, Kochi, Kerala''': Opened in 2015, this hospital is located on a 40-acre campus in Kochi, Kerala. At present, it is a 1745 bed quaternary care healthcare centre in a 40-acre campus.{{cite web |date=10 November 2014 |title=Medcity — A big relief for advanced stage patients |url=http://www.khaleejtimes.com/mobile/inside.asp?xfile=/data/international/2014/November/international_November202.xml§ion=international |accessdate=4 July 2015 |publisher=Khaleej Times}} * '''Aster Pharmacy''': Established in 1989, it operates a network of pharmacies across India.{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Aster Pharmacy bags the SKEA Awards for the second time |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/aster-pharmacy-bags-the-skea-awards-for-the-second-time |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=Khaleej Times |language=en}} * '''Aster Labs:''' Formerly known as Aster Diagnostic Centre, this division provides diagnostic services and operates a laboratory in Bengaluru, along with 20 satellite laboratories and over 190 patient service centres across several Indian states. It offers a range of medical tests.{{Cite web |title=Outlook India Magazine Online- Read News India, Latest News Analysis, World, Sports, Entertainment {{!}} Best Online Magazine India |url=https://www.outlookindia.com/ |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=Outlook India |language=en}} * '''Dr. Moopen’s Medical College, Wayanad, Kerala:''' A medical college in Wayanad offering undergraduate and postgraduate programs in medicine, nursing, and pharmacy.{{Cite news |last= |first= |last2= |last3= |first3= |date=3 April 2022 |title=Dr Moopen's College On Revamp Mode |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/dr-moopens-college-on-revamp-mode/articleshow/90617206.cms |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}{{Cite news |last= |first= |last2= |last3= |first3= |date=8 April 2012 |title=Medical college in Wayanad soon |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/education/news/medical-college-in-wayanad-soon/articleshow/12576098.cms |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=The Times of India |language=en}} * '''Aster Health Academy''': An initiative for healthcare education and professional training.{{Cite web |title=Aster Health Academy partners with national institutions, universities to offer advanced medical courses |url=https://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/education/aster-health-academy-partners-with-national-institutions-universities-to-offer-advanced-medical-courses/113135594 |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=ETHealthworld.com |language=en}} == Community initiatives == === Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award === The Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award (AGGNA) was established in 2022 to recognize nurses in areas such as patient care, leadership, education, community service, and healthcare innovation.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-04 |title=Now, Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award '23 in London - Healthcare Radius |url=https://www.healthcareradius.in/events/now-aster-guardians-global-nursing-award-23-in-london |access-date=2025-11-15 |language=en-US}} The first award was presented in Dubai in May 2022 to [[Anna Qabale Duba]] of [[Jomo Kenyatta|Kenya]].{{Cite news |date=2022-05-13 |title=Kenyan fighting FGM crowned world's best nurse |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-61435153 |access-date=2025-11-15 |language=en-GB}} The second edition took place in London in May 2023, with Margaret Helen Shepherd from the United Kingdom receiving the award.{{Cite web |title=Margaret Helen Shepherd from the UK bags Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2023 |url=https://health.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/industry/margaret-helen-shepherd-from-the-uk-bags-aster-guardians-global-nursing-award-2023/100249840 |access-date=2025-11-15 |website=ETHealthworld.com |language=en}} The third edition was held in Bengaluru in November 2024, with over 78,000 applicants from more than 200 countries. Winners are selected by an independent jury, with [[Ernst & Young|Ernst & Young LLP]] serving as the external evaluation partner.{{Cite news |date=2023-10-01 |title=Aster DM Healthcare invites nominations for Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award-2024 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/aster-dm-healthcare-invites-nominations-for-aster-guardians-global-nursing-award-2024/article67369838.ece |access-date=2025-11-15 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} == See also == * [[Health care provider]] == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|https://www.asterdmhealthcare.in}} [[Category:Companies established in 1987]] [[Category:Health care companies of India]] [[Category:Health care companies established in 1987]] [[Category:Hospital networks in India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
extract: Aster DM Healthcare Limited is an Indian healthcare company founded by Azad Moopen in 1987. The company is registered in Bengaluru, which became the headquarters for its India operations following the separation of its Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) business in 2024. Aster operates a network of hospitals, clinics, pharmacies, and diagnostic centres across several Indian states.
